gamerule.spacehorizons.vacuum_damage.des: Players suffocate in a vacuum (airless planets and above the atmosphere) when their oxygen runs out
death.attack.spacehorizons_vacuum: %1$s suffocated in the vacuum of space
death.attack.spacehorizons_vacuum.player: %1$s suffocated in the vacuum of space whilst trying to escape %2$s
advancements.spacehorizons.root.title: Look Up
advancements.spacehorizons.root.descript: A faint, steady signal is coming from the Moon. Too regular to be natural.
advancements.spacehorizons.steel_blend.d: Mix 1 iron ingot with 2 coal. Iron alone will not reach the Moon.
advancements.spacehorizons.steel_ingot.d: Smelt the steel blend in a blast furnace.
Forge a hammer out of steel ingots.
advancements.spacehorizons.steel_plate.d: Hammer two steel ingots into a plate.
advancements.spacehorizons.basic_circuit: Assemble a basic circuit. The signal needs something to listen with.
advancements.spacehorizons.refinery.desc: Build a refinery to turn coal into rocket fuel.
advancements.spacehorizons.fuel_full.des: Fill a canister with 1000 mB of rocket fuel.
advancements.spacehorizons.oxygen_compre: Build an oxygen compressor. It squeezes breathable air into a tank, and does nothing where there is no air.
advancements.spacehorizons.oxygen_full.d: Fill an oxygen tank to the brim with breathable air.
advancements.spacehorizons.steel_block.d: Compress nine steel ingots into a block of steel.
advancements.spacehorizons.suit_up.title: Sealed In
advancements.spacehorizons.suit_up.descr: Wear the full space suit: helmet, chestplate, leggings and boots. Without all four, the vacuum is cold.
Breathe in a vacuum for 30 seconds on your suit's oxygen tank alone.
jei.spacehorizons.compression.fuel: Burns furnace fuel only while compressing (1 coal fills %s small tanks)
jei.spacehorizons.info.oxygen_tank_small: Holds 2 minutes of breathing for use in a vacuum. Craft it from 5 steel plates, 1 copper ingot and 1 glass pane, and fill it in an oxygen compressor (breathable air only).
jei.spacehorizons.info.oxygen_tank_large: Holds 6 minutes of breathing, three times the small tank. Craft it from 7 steel plates, 1 copper ingot and 1 glass pane, and fill it in an oxygen compressor (breathable air only).
jei.spacehorizons.info.fuel_canister: Craft it from 5 steel plates and 1 steel nugget. Put it in the refinery's canister slot: it fills with rocket fuel (up to 1000 mB) to carry it around.
jei.spacehorizons.info.forge_hammer: Craft it from 4 steel ingots and 2 sticks. Use it as an ingredient (for example, to make steel plates): it is not consumed, but loses 1 durability per craft.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ship_bridge: The core that defines a ship. Click it inside a ship in the shipyard to see the ship's mass, thrust, Δv and fuel. Craft it around a rocket cockpit.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ship_impulse_engi: Pushes the ship forward. Every impulse engine in the ship adds thrust (more thrust than a rocket engine, with less fuel efficiency). The nozzle points to the stern.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ship_window: Glass that shows the universe outside: the sky turns with the ship's attitude.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ship_seat: The pilot's seat: right-click to sit and take the controls (same keys as the rocket). Other players walk freely inside the ship.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ship_airlock: A one-block hatch: right-click to open and close it. Stack two to make a doorway.

message.spacehorizons.ship.bridge_outsid: The bridge only commands a ship inside the shipyard (ground assembly comes later).
message.spacehorizons.ship.bridge_no_shi: This bridge is not inside a registered ship.
message.spacehorizons.ship.descent_refus: Descent refused: someone is standing inside the ship. Everyone aboard must sit down.
message.spacehorizons.ship.descent_no_bo: Descent refused: this world has no dimension for that planet.
message.spacehorizons.ship.assembled: Ship assembled: %s blocks, %s t dry mass, %s mB of fuel. You are at the helm.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.assembled: Rocket assembled: %s blocks, %s t dry mass, %s mB of fuel. Click it to sit; Shift + click takes it apart again.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.landed: Rocket taken apart: %s blocks are back in place.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.no_cockpit: The rocket has to be assembled from its cockpit.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.multiple_co: A rocket can have only one cockpit (found %s).
message.spacehorizons.rocket.no_tank: The rocket has no fuel tank.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.no_pad: The rocket has to stand on a launch pad.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.no_liftoff_: No engine to lift off: it needs an impulse engine with its nozzle down, or a rocket engine.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.too_large: The rocket is too large (at most %s blocks, 128 wide and deep, 256 tall).
message.spacehorizons.rocket.touches_ter: The rocket touches the terrain at %s, %s, %s. Only the launch pad may touch it.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.forbidden_b: A block at %s, %s, %s cannot be part of a rocket (bedrock, fluid, spawner...).
message.spacehorizons.rocket.unloaded_ch: Part of the rocket is in an unloaded chunk (%s, %s, %s).
message.spacehorizons.rocket.packet_too_: The rocket is too detailed to be sent over the network (more than 16 MiB).
message.spacehorizons.rocket.space_occup: There is no room to put the rocket back: the block at %s, %s, %s is in the way.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.not_upright: The rocket is tilted too much (%s degrees) to be taken apart.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.not_landed: The rocket has to be landed to be taken apart.
message.spacehorizons.rocket.not_allowed: You are not allowed to change the blocks at %s, %s, %s.

screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.title: Rocket Blueprints
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.locked_hi: Lost in an abandoned base on the Moon. Available in creative for now.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.hint.subo: 1x1 engine, 1x1x8 tank column, cockpit and parachute: goes above the atmosphere and comes back down.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.hint.orbi: 2x2x2 engine, 1x1x4 tank column, cockpit and parachute: reaches orbit.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.hint.luna: 3x3 engine layer, 3x3x5 tank column, cockpit, parachute and hull: Moon, landing and return.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.blank_hin: Then use it on a launch pad with a rocket on it.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.help1: Use the blueprint on a launch pad: a hologram shows where each block goes.
screen.spacehorizons.blueprint.help2: Missing = ghost, wrong = red, right = disappears. It is a suggestion: build as you like.

jei.spacehorizons.info.nuclear_engine: Nuclear thermal engine: twice the Isp of the chemical engine, with less thrust per ton. Burns hydrogen (hydrogen tank above it) while the core lasts: use a nuclear fuel rod on it to load one engine block (each rod heats 32,000 mB of hydrogen). Forms 2x2x2 and 3x3x3 like the chemical engine.
jei.spacehorizons.info.ion_engine: Ion engine: huge Isp and tiny thrust, it lifts off from no planet; it works in space. Burns xenon (xenon tank above it) with power from RTG generators on the rocket: the 1x1 needs 1 generator, the 2x2x2 needs 6 and the 3x3x3 needs 16; with fewer it pushes in proportion.
jei.spacehorizons.info.fusion_engine: Fusion engine: high Isp and high thrust, the top of the progression. Burns the helium-3 it stores itself (1,000 mB per block): use a helium-3 canister on it to load. Needs no tank.
jei.spacehorizons.info.hydrogen_tank: Holds 4,000 mB of hydrogen per block. Like the fuel tank, it forms columns 1 to 3 wide and 4 to 12 tall (seamless, with less hull per block). Fill it with the hydrogen canister.
jei.spacehorizons.info.xenon_tank: Holds 4,000 mB of xenon per block (dense gas under pressure). Forms columns like the fuel tank. Fill it with the xenon canister.
jei.spacehorizons.info.rtg_generator: Radioisotope generator: the power for the ion engine. Each generator on the rocket powers one 1x1 ion engine (the 2x2x2 needs 6, the 3x3x3 needs 16).
jei.spacehorizons.info.mars_regolith: Martian soil. Without silk touch it sometimes drops rare earth dust (like gravel drops flint).
jei.spacehorizons.info.nuclear_fuel_rod: Thorium rod from Martian rare earths. Use it on a nuclear engine to load an empty engine block: it heats 32,000 mB of hydrogen. It is also the heat source of the RTG generator.
jei.spacehorizons.info.rare_earth_dust: Comes from Martian regolith. Used for nuclear rods, superconductor coils and the ion engine.
jei.spacehorizons.info.hydrogen_canister: Liquid hydrogen for the nuclear engine (1,000 mB). Fill it at a crafting table: canister + 2 water buckets + 1 redstone (electrolysis). Pour it into a hydrogen tank.
jei.spacehorizons.info.xenon_canister: Xenon for the ion engine (1,000 mB). Fill it at a crafting table: canister + 4 Martian regolith + 1 rare earth dust (gas trapped in the regolith). Pour it into a xenon tank.
jei.spacehorizons.info.antigravity_gener: Lets the ship anchor in mid-air: with a charged generator, standing still and nothing touching it, the anchor key turns the ship into blocks. Anchoring spends the charge (no fuel); it comes back by itself after 20 s while the block is in the world (anchored or landed ship).
hud.spacehorizons.anchor.title: Anchor
message.spacehorizons.anchor.not_ship: Only ships built from the bridge can anchor in mid-air (and not in space).
message.spacehorizons.anchor.no_generato: Cannot anchor: the ship needs an antigravity generator.
message.spacehorizons.anchor.no_energy: Cannot anchor: the antigravity generator is empty. It recharges while the ship is anchored or landed.
message.spacehorizons.anchor.no_room: Cannot anchor: blocks are touching the ship (marked in red).
message.spacehorizons.anchor.too_fast: Cannot anchor: the ship has to be standing still.
message.spacehorizons.anchor.too_tilted: Cannot anchor: the ship is tilted too much.
message.spacehorizons.anchor.parachute: Cannot anchor with the parachute open.
gui.spacehorizons.moonbase.status.blocke: No free side for the air
advancements.spacehorizons.solar_power.d: Build a solar panel. It only makes power while the sun is up and nothing covers it; chain panels, batteries and machines face to face (or with cables).
advancements.spacehorizons.lunar_ice.des: Mine lunar ice. It hides under the floors of craters near the lunar poles.
advancements.spacehorizons.sealed_room.d: Breathe inside a sealed room pressurized by an oxygen generator, without a helmet.
Build a helium-3 extractor: regolith in, fusion fuel out.
advancements.spacehorizons.moon_electrol: Build an electrolyzer: lunar ice becomes hydrogen and oxygen.
advancements.spacehorizons.moon_fuel.des: Build a lunar refinery and turn lunar ice into rocket fuel to return to Earth.
jei.spacehorizons.info.lunar_ice_ore: Water ice under the floors of craters at high latitudes of the Moon (55 degrees or more). Without silk touch it drops 1 to 3 lunar ice.
jei.spacehorizons.info.lunar_ice: Feeds the electrolyzer (hydrogen and oxygen), the lunar refinery (rocket fuel: 400 mB each) and the oxygen generator (1,200 breathing ticks each).
jei.spacehorizons.info.solar_panel: Makes up to 8 UE/t with the sun high and the sky clear; nothing at night or when covered. Power passes face to face between panels, batteries, cables and machines. Right-click shows the power.
jei.spacehorizons.info.battery: Stores 200,000 UE. Gives power to cables and machines next to it and balances with other batteries.
jei.spacehorizons.info.power_cable: Carries power through a line of blocks (1,000 UE buffer). Panels, batteries and machines connect by touching faces; the cable only extends the reach.
jei.spacehorizons.info.oxygen_generator: Pressurizes the sealed room around it: needs walls of full blocks (glass counts; doors must be closed), at most 1,000 blocks of air, 4 UE/t and oxygen from a tank or lunar ice. Open a door or break a wall and the room leaks within seconds. Inside, you breathe without a suit tank and do not freeze.
jei.spacehorizons.info.helium3_extractor: Turns regolith blocks (the lunar soil) into helium-3 in a canister: 250 mB per block in 2 s at 10 UE/t. Works only on the Moon.
jei.spacehorizons.info.electrolyzer: Splits lunar ice: 500 mB of hydrogen (into a hydrogen canister) and 1,200 breathing ticks of oxygen (into an oxygen tank) per ice, in 5 s at 20 UE/t.
jei.spacehorizons.info.lunar_refinery: Turns lunar ice into Tier 1 rocket fuel (400 mB per ice, 6 s, 30 UE/t) in a fuel canister. Ten ice fill a rocket tank.
jei.spacehorizons.info.helium3_canister: Helium-3 for the fusion engine (1,000 mB). Only on the Moon: use the canister on the lunar ground to process the regolith (the block is consumed and the canister gains 125 mB; 8 blocks fill it). Pour it into a fusion engine.
story.spacehorizons.voss_01.title: Day 1: the pulse
story.spacehorizons.voss_01.author: Dr. Helena Voss
story.spacehorizons.voss_01.body:
Day 1. Small hours at the Aurora Observatory. The hydrogen receiver picked up a pulse that should not exist: short, clean, always every 7 minutes and 12 seconds. I ran the whole pulsar catalogue. None of them match that rhythm.

The strangest part is the direction. It is not coming from deep space: it comes from the Moon. From the face that looks at us, near the middle of the disc. The Moon does not pulse, Tomas. Something up there is switched on.

I will leave the receiver recording all night. If it is instrument noise, tomorrow I will laugh about it.
story.spacehorizons.voss_02.title: Day 9: the map
story.spacehorizons.voss_02.author: Dr. Helena Voss
story.spacehorizons.voss_02.body:
Day 9. It was not noise. After eight days of recording the pulse showed its trick: every 17 pulses the rhythm changes and the signal carries a table. It took me three nights to see it is not text, it is a map. Five points on the lunar surface, the first a few hundred metres from where the signal seems to be born.

I asked the board for funding. Answer: observatories do not send rockets, observatories listen. So we will go ourselves. Tomas drew a rocket with what the workshop allows and I left the plans in the archive terminal. Whoever comes here after us: the terminal has everything, including where to land.

If the signal is an invitation, I intend to accept.
story.spacehorizons.aurora_terminal.body:
AURORA OBSERVATORY, TEAM ARCHIVE

SIGNAL: 7 min 12 s pulse on the hydrogen line (1,420 MHz).
SOURCE: the Earth-facing side of the Moon.
STATUS: field team (H. Voss, T. Reyes) left for the Moon. No contact since day 41.

ATTACHMENTS RELEASED:
1. Blueprint of the orbital training rocket, the first the team built.
2. A compass tuned to Selene-1 Base, the first point on the map. It only points while you are on the Moon.

Note from H. Voss: "Bring spare fuel. The Moon does not return favours."
story.spacehorizons.reyes_01.title: Day 14: Selene-1
story.spacehorizons.reyes_01.author: Eng. Tomas Reyes
story.spacehorizons.reyes_01.body:
Day 14. We arrived in one piece, which is more than I bet on. We landed about five hundred metres from the marked point and dragged everything by hand. We built the base in eleven days: three modules, a control room and the oxygen compressor running in a cycle.

I named it Selene-1. Helena laughed at the name but let it be.

The walls hold the air. What they cannot hold is our urge to go to the signal point. Tomorrow we go out in suits.
story.spacehorizons.reyes_02.title: Day 31: the air
story.spacehorizons.reyes_02.author: Eng. Tomas Reyes
story.spacehorizons.reyes_02.body:
Day 31. The air ran out before the fuel, and I got the sums wrong. The compressor drew more than the generator delivered, a seal gave way in module two and the rest was bad arithmetic.

We survived because Helena shut the hatch in time. We lost the module and gained a warning: the signal does NOT come from the base. It is a few hundred metres away, at a spot where the dust looks different. She says it looks like wreckage.

The lunar rocket blueprint is in the control room terminal. If I do not come back, whoever finds this takes the blueprint and goes home the same way.
story.spacehorizons.selene_terminal.body:
SELENE-1 BASE, MASTER LOG

STATUS: abandoned. Module 2 breached. Oxygen reserve at zero. Generator down.
LAST ENTRY: day 44. H. Voss went on foot to the signal point. T. Reyes stayed at control and lost contact at 04:12.

ATTACHMENTS RELEASED:
1. Lunar rocket blueprint (landing and return, with the reinforced hull).
2. A compass tuned to the wreckage of the Vigia-3 probe, the source of the signal.

ENGINEER'S NOTE: "Whoever gets here: the rocket in the blueprint came home once. Just not with me."
story.spacehorizons.voss_03.title: Day 44: the echo
story.spacehorizons.voss_03.author: Dr. Helena Voss
story.spacehorizons.voss_03.body:
Day 44. I am at the probe. Twelve minutes by suit from the base. A burnt hull, a half-buried antenna dish and a worn seal where you can still read VIGIA.

It is a probe from generations ago: it crashed here and stayed on with the last generator it had left. And it is not speaking on its own. It is repeating. Something talks to it, and it only gives back the echo.

I will read the telemetry on its terminal. If the echo has an address, I want to know where it points.
story.spacehorizons.vigia_terminal.title: Probe telemetry
story.spacehorizons.vigia_terminal.body:
VIGIA-3 PROBE, RECOVERED TELEMETRY

MISSION: inner system reconnaissance.
STATE: hull compromised, high-gain antenna functional, power: RTG at 3%.

LINK LOG: Vigia-3 does not originate the 7 min 12 s pulse. It RETRANSMITS a beam received from beyond Earth and Moon. Beam origin: MARS, plain north of the equator, near x 3000, z -1500.

The five-point map is the relay route: the other four points are on Mars.

WARNING: the orbital or lunar rocket cannot take a crew there. It needs more delta-v.
story.spacehorizons.mars_hook.title: For whoever comes next
story.spacehorizons.mars_hook.author: Dr. Helena Voss
story.spacehorizons.mars_hook.body:
For whoever comes next. If you read the telemetry, you already know: the signal is not from the Moon. It is from Mars, and whoever speaks there knows our language of pulses.

Tomas says that with what exists today I cannot get there. He is right, and I will try anyway. I noted what is missing: engines beyond chemical, fuel that is not just coal and faith, and materials I only know by name. Titanium. Helium-3. All of that lies on the other side.

If you pass through Mars and find my flag, leave a light on. I will need to find my way back.

advancements.spacehorizons.story_observa: Read one of Helena Voss's journals in the abandoned research station. Look for a rusted dish on dry land.
advancements.spacehorizons.story_coordin: Use the observatory terminal and take the orbital blueprint and the lunar base compass.
Read one of Tomas Reyes's journals in the abandoned lunar base.
advancements.spacehorizons.story_lunar_p: Take the lunar rocket blueprint from the Selene-1 base terminal.
advancements.spacehorizons.story_probe.d: Read the fallen probe's telemetry: it only repeats a signal.
advancements.spacehorizons.story_mars.de: Read Helena's last note: the signal comes from Mars, and Mars asks for more than a lunar rocket.
